content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To make buckeyes, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Soften the butter at room temperature (45 minutes)
Step 2. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper (2 minutes)
Step 3. Measure out the creamy peanut butter (3 minutes)
Step 4. Sift the powdered sugar into a large bowl (10 minutes)
Step 5. Mix the butter and peanut butter together (5 minutes)
Step 6. Melt the chocolate wafers in a double boiler (12 minutes)
Step 7. Clear space in the freezer for the baking sheet (5 minutes)
Step 8. Gather all necessary measuring cups and spoons (2 minutes)
Step 9. Temper the melted chocolate to a smooth consistency (8 minutes)
Step 10. Take the ingredients out of the pantry (4 minutes)
Step 11. Measure the vanilla extract (1 minute)
Step 12. Stir the shortening into the chocolate (3 minutes)
Step 13. Beat the peanut butter mixture until fluffy (6 minutes)
Step 14. Blend the softened butter into the sugar (8 minutes)
Step 15. Roll the dough into one-inch balls (20 minutes)
Step 16. Whisk the chocolate to remove any lumps (2 minutes)
Step 17. Wash and dry the mixing bowls (10 minutes)
Step 18. Combine the peanut butter with the vanilla (4 minutes)
Step 19. Wipe down the kitchen counters (10 minutes)
Step 20. Plug in the electric hand mixer (30 seconds)
Step 21. Prepare a clean surface for rolling dough (5 minutes)
Step 22. Scrape the sides of the mixing bowl (1 minute)
Step 23. Test the chocolate temperature with a thermometer (1 minute)
Step 24. Set up the dipping station with toothpicks (5 minutes)
Step 25. Chill the dough balls in the refrigerator (30 minutes)
Step 26. Gradually add the peanut butter mixture to the sugar (7 minutes)
Step 27. Put away the extra bags of sugar (3 minutes)
Step 28. Crack a fresh container of salt for a tiny pinch (1 minute)
Step 29. Retrieve the baking sheet from the cupboard (1 minute)
Step 30. Clean the cooling rack (5 minutes)
Step 31. Arrange the dipping tools on the counter (2 minutes)
Step 32. Finely chop the chocolate for faster melting (10 minutes)
Step 33. Place the parchment paper onto the tray (1 minute)
Step 34. Check the inventory of toothpicks (1 minute)
Step 35. Measure the total weight of the dough (2 minutes)
Step 36. Label the storage containers (4 minutes)
Step 37. Knead the dough by hand to ensure smoothness (5 minutes)
Step 38. Open the jar of peanut butter (30 seconds)
Step 39. Melt a small amount of paraffin wax if using (10 minutes)
Step 40. Dip each ball into the chocolate using a toothpick (25 minutes)
